questions.prompt: Match each fire to the safest way to put it out.

pairs.right: Turn off gas and cover with a lid
Switch off power, use a CO₂ extinguisher

questions.explain: Match the method to the fuel: never water on oil, petrol or electrical fires.

questions.prompt: Why is water NOT used to put out an electrical fire?
options: Water conducts electricity and could cause a shock
Water adds fuel
Water makes more smoke
Water is too heavy
questions.explain: Water conducts electricity, so there is a serious risk of electric shock.

questions.prompt: How does a CO₂ fire extinguisher control a fire?
options: CO₂ is a fuel that burns away the fire
CO₂ is heavier than air and blankets the fire, cutting off oxygen; it also cools it
CO₂ makes the fire hotter so it burns out quickly
CO₂ reacts with the flame to make water
questions.explain: CO₂ smothers the fire (removes oxygen) and cools the fuel.

questions.prompt: Someone's clothes catch fire. Put the actions in order.
steps: Roll to smother the flames (or wrap in a blanket)
Cool the burn with running water
questions.explain: Stop, drop and roll cuts off oxygen; then cool the burn and get help.

questions.prompt: You smell LPG in the kitchen. What should you do? Choose all that apply.
options: Turn off the regulator
Open doors and windows
Switch on the light to look for the leak
Avoid using any switches or flames
Call the gas agency's emergency number
questions.explain: Remove the fuel, let the gas escape, and avoid sparks. Switching on a light could ignite the gas.

questions.prompt: Why should you crawl low when escaping a smoky room?
options: It looks safer
It is faster
Hot smoke rises, so cleaner, cooler air is near the floor
Fire can't reach the floor
questions.explain: Hot smoke and gases rise; the air near the floor is easier to breathe.

questions.prompt: Why is fanning a small fire a bad idea?
options: It cools the fire too much
It supplies more oxygen, making the fire bigger
It adds carbon dioxide
It removes the fuel
questions.explain: Moving air brings fresh oxygen, feeding the fire.

questions.text: In India, you can call ___ for the fire brigade or ___ for any emergency.
questions.explain: 101 = fire; 112 = national emergency number (100 is police, 108 is ambulance).

questions.prompt: Explain, using the fire triangle, why a kitchen oil fire should be covered with a lid rather than put out with water.
questions.modelAnswer: Covering the pan with a lid cuts off the oxygen side of the fire triangle, so the fire goes out safely. Water is dangerous because it sinks under the hot oil, instantly boils into steam and throws burning oil out, spreading the fire.
rubric: I said the lid cuts off oxygen
I explained what water does (sinks, boils, spreads burning oil)
I referred to the fire triangle
questions.explain: Use the fire triangle to choose the safe side to remove.
